items.title: A natural depsipeptide antibiotic binds the E-site of the bacterial ribosome
items.summary: Improved fractionation strategies can identify antibiotics with previously unseen scaffolds and mechanisms, exemplified by manikomycin from Streptomyces rimosus, which acts by targeting the E-site of the bacterial large ribosomal subunit.

items.title: ‘Transformative’ CAR-T therapy allows three people to receive kidney transplants
items.summary: They had ‘highly sensitized’ immune systems that usually reject donated organs, leaving them with few options for survival.

items.title: This mysterious lung disease affects millions of people — but a drug tested in mice shows promise
items.summary: The therapy activates a protein that could stop pulmonary fibrosis from progressing.

items.title: Relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and beyond
items.summary: NASA’s Juno observations show relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and establish a universal scaling law linking shock size to maximum cosmic ray energy.

items.title: Mining triggers extensive additional deforestation in sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: Extensive mining activity leads to large-scale deforestation of dense tropical forests across sub-Saharan Africa, driven particularly by key energy transition minerals such as cobalt.

items.title: Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein in maize
items.summary: Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein without lowering crop yield when expressed in modern maize, providing a powerful strategy for crop improvement to meet future population demands.

items.title: Commensal-derived acetylcholine enhances mucosal immune education
items.summary: A diet–microbiome–host axis strengthens mucosal immune defences and reinforces host–microbiota mutualism.

items.title: Jupiter observations reveal a simple scaling law for particle acceleration
items.summary: Supersonic shocks in the vicinity of Jupiter suggest that transient plasma structures could govern the acceleration of particles travelling through space.

items.title: How a rush for minerals is causing deforestation in tropical regions
items.summary: An analysis of the extent to which mining caused deforestation between 2001 and 2020 in areas near mines in sub-Saharan Africa could help conservation efforts.

items.title: White House proposes vast overhaul of US science funding: what you need to know
items.summary: The Trump administration’s proposal aims to improve transparency in federal funding, but critics fear the proposed rules would politicize research

items.title: Your phone can use tiny skin-colour changes to measure your heart rate
items.summary: Passive heart-rate monitoring during regular phone use could provide early warning of health issues — plus, testing Richard Feynman’s solution to the ‘restaurant dilemma’ problem.

items.title: Acquired genetic and cell-state changes in IDH-mutant glioma progression
items.summary: Longitudinal transcriptomic, chromatin and genomic analyses of the two types of IDH-mutant glioma reveal in detail how disease progression is influenced by interdependent genetic, epigenetic and microenvironmental factors.

items.title: Cold-induced peptide signalling secures pollen resilience and crop yield
items.summary: A small-peptide signalling axis involving RGF family members controls resilience to cold stress in tomatoes and rice; modulating this pathway prevents cold-induced yield losses.

items.title: Spermine is an endogenous iron chelator that inhibits ferroptosis
items.summary: A non-canonical metabolic route for spermine synthesis mediated by ALDH18A1 limits iron availability and lipid peroxidation in hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.title: Chiral superfluorescence from perovskite superlattices at room temperature
items.summary: Chiral perovskite superlattices exhibit room-temperature circularly polarized superfluorescence, with emission intensity and polarization controllable by weak magnetic fields.

items.title: LASER couples damage sensing to ESCRT assembly for lysosome repair
items.summary: ATG8 conjugation on damaged lysosomes triggers rapid assembly of a protein complex containing TFG, which directs lysosomal membrane repair by recruiting ESCRT proteins to sites of damage.

items.title: High-fidelity modular skeletons authenticate a Cambrian origin for Bryozoa
items.summary: Exquisite early Cambrian fossils of Protomelission gatehousei and Dayingomelission hexaclitia preserve soft-tissue anatomy and skeletal microstructure, confirming that these taxa are definitively bryozoans and indicating a deeper origin for the Bryozoa than was first apparent.

items.title: Centromeric footprints preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancers
items.summary: Centromeric DNA repeat insertions and CENP-A chromatin assembly are identified as genomic signatures that preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancer cells.

items.title: Queen cell architecture shapes honey bee queen development
items.summary: Worker bee construction behaviour actively engineers a physicochemical niche that is crucial for queen development in honey bees.

items.title: A maize gene that coordinates flowering aids drought resistance
items.summary: The synchronous flowering of male and female flower clusters in maize is crucial, but drought disrupts this synchrony, leading to considerable yield losses. A gene called SAUR72 is shown to preserve flowering synchrony in drought conditions, offering a potential strategy for breeding drought-resilient maize varieties.

items.title: Can an army of babies and dogs rescue psychology from its reproducibility crisis?
items.summary: Labs are teaming up to run a host of huge projects that aim to bring rigour to cognitive science.

items.title: Nanostructure of tooth enamel casts light on dietary shifts as humans evolved
items.summary: The arrangement of mineral nanocrystals in the tooth enamel of primates, hominins and modern humans altered as the diet of these species changed.

items.title: Ubiquitin tags detected on non-protein biomolecules using new method
items.summary: An innovative method of mass spectrometry has detected the small protein ubiquitin on biomolecules other than proteins. In mouse liver, the energy-storing molecule glycogen has a large increase in ubiquitination — involving 1% of the liver’s total ubiquitin — during fasting, when glycogen is broken down.

items.title: Device could sniff out fusion reactors secretly making material for a nuclear bomb
items.summary: Antineutrinos made alongside the production of weapons-grade plutonium could be spotted with existing technology.

items.title: Cell-type-resolved genetic variation shapes inflammatory bowel disease risk
items.summary: Single-cell mapping of cis-expression quantitative trait loci in inflammatory bowel disease revealed distal, enhancer-enriched variants detected at the cell-type level more frequently co-localize with genome-wide association study loci than those identified at the tissue level.

items.title: Plastoglobules compartmentalize nitrogen assimilation in maize
items.summary: Chloroplast plastoglobules act as nitrogen-assimilation hubs in maize, with key enzymes enhancing nitrogen-use efficiency and offering new strategies for developing high-yield, sustainable crops.

items.title: Mechanophore cross-linking enhances ballistic energy dissipation of polymers
items.summary: Embedding a small fraction of force-sensitive mechanophores as cross-links into common polymers enhances ballistic energy dissipation.

items.title: Nuclear shell structure governs short-range nucleon pairing
items.summary: The scattering of high-energy electrons from three different nuclei demonstrated that short-range-correlated pairing depends far more on the specific quantum orbitals occupied by nucleons than predicted by theoretical models.

items.title: Enamel nanocrystal misorientation increased with meat-eating and agriculture
items.summary: An analysis of enamel nanocrystal misorientation in primate and human teeth across three major dietary shifts in human evolution shows that misorientation increased with harder diets, suggesting that misorientation contributes to enamel’s resilience.

items.title: What a royal bedchamber provides the queen bee
items.summary: When considering what shapes animal development, factors such as genetics come to mind. For a queen bee, however, her special wax home also has a role.

items.title: Microsoft upgrades controversial quantum chip — researchers are still sceptical
items.summary: The tech giant says it will make ‘topological’ quantum computers that can be scaled up faster than competing technologies.

items.title: Tiny hubs of metabolic activity optimize nitrogen use in maize
items.summary: Structures called plastoglobules organize the enzymes that turn nitrogen into compounds needed for plant growth, offering lessons for sustainable agriculture.

items.title: Troubled waters: a plant protein senses when cells are running dry
items.summary: How cells sense fluctuations in the availability of water has long been unclear. The protein SAM8 is now shown to undergo a process called phase separation in a way that depends on its hydration, thereby sensing cellular water availability and linking changes in water status to the regulation of gene expression.

items.title: Babies’ birth weight improves with help of payments to parents
items.summary: Interventions that included home visits and cash transfers led to more strapping infants in an Indian state.

items.summary: The size of tropical vegetation gross primary production

items.title: Earth’s east–west albedo symmetry
items.summary: Analysis of a 25-year satellite record shows that Earth has a persistent east–west albedo symmetry split at 27° E, with clear-sky albedo, cloud radiative effect and open-ocean fraction exhibiting a triple symmetry around this meridian.

items.title: High-pulse-energy integrated mode-locked laser using a Mamyshev oscillator
items.summary: A Mamyshev oscillator mode-locked laser compactly integrated on a photonic-chip delivers nanojoule, femtosecond pulses.

items.title: Cooperation conflicts with equality when allocating public goods
items.summary: Uniform sharing of public goods can boost cooperation in social networks, but often concentrates benefits among well-connected individuals, creating inequality despite greater collective success.

items.title: Recovery of plastic from mixed waste boosts recycling rates but affects quality
items.summary: Recovering plastic packaging from mixed domestic waste, as well as collecting plastic waste already sorted by households, increases recycling volumes but raises contamination and safety risks. Policies that support the sorting of plastics from mixed waste at central facilities should have strict quality standards and investment in advanced purification systems to ensure safe recycling outcomes.

items.title: How good are ‘AI doctors’ — and will they take over medicine?
items.summary: Nature talks to specialists about whether people might soon be diagnosed by artificial-intelligence systems.

items.title: Analysis of trade-offs of post-sorting plastic packaging
items.summary: An analysis of post-sorting plastic packaging shows that target polymer purity is similar across source-separation and post-sorting pathways, but post-sorted plastics contain more contaminants that need to be removed before recyclate production.

items.title: Why a synthetic human genome is still worth building
items.summary: A decade on from the launch of an ambitious project, it’s time to revisit the reasons for constructing a human genome from scratch.

items.title: Science with military applications is cited more than civilian-only research
items.summary: Researchers analysed the scientific impact of dual-use research in US patent records and bibliometric databases.

items.title: Daily briefing: These immune cells go out with a bang
items.summary: Newly-discovered ‘ruptoblasts’ explode to shower nearby cells with toxic chemicals. Plus, how psychology is tackling its reproducibility crisis and when to settle, according to maths.

items.title: What’s behind China’s historically high counts of corresponding authors?
items.summary: From 2016 to 2020, almost one-third of papers by authors in China had multiple corresponding authors — but policy reforms are expected to have dampened the trend.

items.summary: Author Correction: Physiology and immunology of a pig-to-human decedent kidney xenotransplant

items.summary: Discover the strengths, limitations and risks associated with using artificial intelligence in your science job applications.
